(a) The city commission has reviewed this Code for the city and considered the policies, regulations, and standards governing development in the city.
(b) The city commission has great respect for reputable medical practitioners who properly attempt to diagnose and treat pain experienced by their patients.
(c) The city commission has considered the experiences and challenges that counties and municipalities around the state and the country are experiencing regarding the prescribing and dispensing of controlled substances and pain medications to those individuals visiting so-called pain management clinics, sometimes referred to as "pill mills" and find them relevant and informative regarding the protection of the public health, safety and welfare of the citizens of the city.
(d) The city commission notes the legislative enactments of the cities of Buford and Kennesaw, and Cherokee County with regard thereto, including their extensive recitation of findings regarding pill mills from various public bodies in the State of Florida, and find them relevant and informative regarding the protection of the public health, safety and welfare of the citizens of the city.
(e) The city commissions find that these pill mills operating as so-called pain management clinics or facilities often prescribe and/or prescribe and dispense Schedules II, III, and IV controlled substances as those substances are identified in O.C.G.A. §§ 16-13-25—16-13-29, to those claiming pain without performing proper and thorough examinations of said patients and their medical records, without a proper medical diagnosis, and without oversight of licensed medical personnel.
(f) The city commission finds that a typical pill mill operating as so-called pain management clinic or facility prescribes and/or prescribes and dispenses controlled substances and pain medications on-site.
(g) The city commission has reviewed information received from law enforcement officials and find that criminal activity tends to increase in areas where these pill mills operating as so-called pain management clinics or facilities are located.
(h) The city commission has been made aware of reports describing a pipeline of trafficking drugs from these pill mills operating as so-called pain management clinics or facilities in South Florida through the state to users in other states such as Kentucky, West Virginia, and Ohio and find them relevant and informative regarding the protection of the public health, safety and welfare of the citizens of the city.
(i) The city commission finds that prescription drug abuse is a major problem in the state and throughout the United States, and according to the state drug and narcotics agency, deaths due to prescription drug overdoses have surpassed those of all other illicit drugs.
(j) The city commission is aware that state law provides for a prescription medication monitoring program, but it appears that such monitoring system is not operational at the present time.
(k) The city commission finds it is necessary and appropriate to adopt this article to require certain information upon application for a business license by pain management clinics for the protection of the public health, safety and welfare of the citizens of the city.

Physician means a person licensed to practice medicine under or pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 43-34-21.
Physician primarily engaged in treatment of pain means a physician who provides a majority of his or her patients with a written prescription for one or more pain medications.
Practice of pharmacy means interpretation, evaluation, or dispensing of prescription drug orders in the patient's best interest; participation in drug and device selection, drug administration, drug regimen reviews, and drug or drug related research; provision of patient counseling and the provision of those acts or services necessary to provide pharmacy care; performing capillary blood tests and interpreting the results as a means to screen for or monitor disease risk factors and facilitate patient education, and a pharmacist performing such functions shall report the results obtained from such blood tests to the patient's physician of choice; and the responsibility for compounding and labeling of drugs and devices, as defined on O.C.G.A. § 26-4-4, as amended.
Schedule II, III, or IV drugs means the drugs defined in O.C.G.A. § 16-13-26 through and including O.C.G.A. § 16-13-29, as amended.
Sensitive use structure means any structure in the Town Center Overlay District, religious assemblies, a school, a public use, a hospital, a building owned or leased by a hospital authority, or any residence.
(Code 2000, § 22-502; Ord. of 3-4-2013)
567:
(a) Issuance or denial of application. Within 45 days after the filing of a completed application for a pain management business license, the city's planning director or his/her designee shall either issue a license to the applicant or deny a license to the applicant. If an applicant is denied a license, the applicant may file a written appeal from the denial to the city commission within 30 days of such denial. No paid management business license shall be issued during the pendency of any such appeal.
(b) Grant of license. The pain management business license may be granted if:
(1) The application is complete and conforms to all of the provisions of this article.
(2) The required fee has been paid.
(3) The application does not contain a material misrepresentation of fact.
(4) The applicant has fully cooperated in the review of that application.
(5) The following persons have plead not guilty to a felony, have not plead nolo contendre to a felony, and have not been convicted of a felony:
a. If the applicant is an individual, the applicant;
b. If the applicant is a business entity, any of the persons holding a financial or ownership interest in that business entity whether such interest is legal or equitable;
c. If the applicant is a corporation, any of the officers;
d. If the applicant is a limited liability company, any of the managers.
(6) The applicant, if a business entity, is in good standing with the secretary of state.
(7) All criminal background checks have been completed by the city department of public safety or the Gwinnett County police department/Hall County sheriff's department.
(c) Completion date of application. The application for a pain management business license is completed on the date that the city receives the last piece of information or document for such application as required by section 12-512.
(Code 2000, § 22-504; Ord. of 3-4-2013)
